analysis:
Reviewed the two head_text units of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 802-1616). The PR is documentation-only, so no executable code changed in these units. The changed ranges visible in the patch are the date bump, a new paragraph near head lines 684-691 (outside these units), a GLM video description at 818-821 and 837, and the response_format/forced tool_choice paragraph at 884-903.

Security-relevant claims in the documentation, not verified against source:
1. GLM video decoding is now documented as variable-frame-rate tolerant. Frames are timed at i / nominalFrameRate and are not refused. The decoded-frame cap (512 MiB, maximumDecodedBytes) and the VisionMemoryGate reservation are still described as bounding the work, so the availability and DoS posture (TB-007, T-010) appears unchanged. Whether the cap holds for VFR tracks with a large frame count is an implementation question for the Swift source (GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset), which I did not see.
2. A new documented behavior (head line 884 onward): the weight hash published for a GLM load is the manifest aggregate from GLM5NextManagedLoad.verifiedArtifactSHA256. VerifiedWeightHashStore lets later coordinator-mode starts register that hash without re-reading weights while file device, inode, size, mtime and ctime are unchanged. This sits near T-012 and T-027 (weight substitution) and the coordinator weight-hash check. The visible text says the load verifies again before serving. The residual risk is metadata-only freshness: an operator who can restore the same stat tuple, or who swaps content in place, might evade it. That cannot be evaluated from the docs alone, since the code is not in this batch. This is an unverified contract and not a finding.
3. The docs say the response_format and forced tool_choice paths are validated after generation, with no token constraint, and that invalid output returns 422 with no content. This is a consistency claim and has no direct impact on the threat model.

The cache sections (T-041) and the MTP, deadline and calibration prose do not change the SSD cache, HMAC names, TTL or account scoping. No regression is identified from these units.

The next pass should check VerifiedWeightHashStore, ProviderLoop.verifiedGLM5NextWeightHash and GLM5NextManagedLoad for TOCTOU and stat-spoofing weaknesses, and the GLM5NextProcessor VFR video bounds, if the code changes are in scope.
